extracted.intended_audience: Applicants and panel members for ERC individual grants (Starting/Consolidator/Advanced Grants); prospective interviewees
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance describing the ERC two-step evaluation process for individual grants (Step 1: assessment of Extended Synopsis and CV; Step 2: full proposal review and interviews), the substantive evaluation criteria, procedural checks (CoI, referee assignment), and advice for interviewees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflict of Interest (CoI) screening
rubrics_metrics.description: Panel team screens for Conflict of Interest (CoI). Panel members receive the book of abstracts and can declare CoI. ERC uses inhouse developed tools to identify CoI. Excluded reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CoI must be declared by panel members on receipt of abstracts; ERC additionally uses automated/in-house tools to detect conflicts; reviewers with CoI are excluded from handling/reviewing the proposal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignment of proposals and workload distribution
rubrics_metrics.description: Assignment of proposals (keywords and abstract) and distribution of workload. Potential proposal transfer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Panel Chair/team assigns proposals to panel members based on keywords/abstracts and balances workload; proposals may be transferred between panels where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Panel briefing and reminder of rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Briefing of Panel Members: Reminder of evaluation criteria and rules; Explanation of evaluation steps.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Panel members receive briefing at start of evaluations to ensure consistent application of criteria and to explain procedural steps (remote evaluation, meetings, referee assignment, scoring and commenting).

rubrics_metrics.name: Step 1 scope (what is evaluated in Step 1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Panel members evaluate remotely the Extended Synopsis of the proposal and the CV (only Part B1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Step 1 is a remote assessment limited to Part B1 (Extended Synopsis) and the PI's CV; reviewers should focus evaluation on intellectual capacity/track record and the synopsis content when forming initial scores and invitations to Step 2.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intellectual capacity and creativity (PI evaluation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Intellectual capacity and creativity: To what extent has the PI demonstrated the ability to conduct ground-breaking research? To what extent does the PI provide evidence of creative and original thinking? To what extent does the PI have the required scientific expertise and capacity to successfully execute the project?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess the PI's track-record, originality, demonstrated leadership in research, and demonstrated capability to carry out high-risk/high-gain projects. Evidence can include publications, previous projects, indicators of creativity and independence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ground‑breaking nature, ambition, and feasibility (research excellence)
rubrics_metrics.description: Ground‑breaking nature, ambition, and feasibility: To what extent does the proposed research address important challenges? To what extent are the objectives ambitious and beyond the state of the art (e.g., novel concepts and approaches or development between or across disciplines)? To what extent is the outlined scientific approach feasible bearing in mind the ground‑breaking nature and ambition of the proposed research?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate the novelty and ambition relative to the field, potential to open new directions, and whether the proposed approach is realistic given the high-risk/high-reward aims. Balance ambition with plausibility and scientific rationale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriateness of research methodology and working arrangements
rubrics_metrics.description: To what extent are the proposed research methodology and working arrangements appropriate to achieve the goals of the project?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the methods, technical approaches, project design, and team/organisational arrangements are well matched to the objectives. Look for sound experimental/analytical plans and suitable collaborations or resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timescales, resources and PI commitment
rubrics_metrics.description: To what extent are the proposed timescales, resources, and PI commitment adequate and properly justified?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examine the realism and justification of the requested budget, timeline, and the PI's time commitment; ensure resources are sufficient and justified for the proposed ambitious work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Step 2 scope (what is evaluated in Step 2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Panel Members AND Remote Referees (experts) evaluate remotely the full scientific proposal (Part B1, Part B2 & Proposal budget).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Step 2 involves external expert referees plus panel members reviewing the full submission including detailed scientific case (Part B2) and budget; evaluations should incorporate referee input and full proposal detail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remote referee recruitment and use
rubrics_metrics.description: Panel team contacts suggested remote referees. Panel team contacts panel members for additional names if suggested reviewers decline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Remote referees are recruited by the panel team using applicant suggestions and panel member proposals; their independent expertise is used to inform Step 2 evaluations and panel discussion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Panel meeting activities: discussion, scoring, commenting, and ranking
rubrics_metrics.description: During panel meetings: Briefing by the panel team and ERC President; Discussion of all proposals; Scoring and ranking of proposals; Writing panel comments; Assignment of remote referees; Panel recommendations for scientific council.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Panel meetings are used to discuss reviews, agree scores and rankings, draft panel comments for feedback, and decide which proposals are invited to interview or recommended for funding; clear, evidence-based commenting is expected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interview presentation and defence (Step 2 interviews)
rubrics_metrics.description: Have clear and representative slides and focus on RESEARCH project! Don’t try to make a business presentation – you are talking to passionate scientists. Get panel interested in YOUR ideas & proposal; Present & defend YOUR ideas (panels want to see that these are your ideas); Don't over-explain your CV! Provide additional preliminary data if available. Anticipate questions. Know the details of your proposal and methods, as well as your research area – who are your main competitors/collaborators? Follow the instructions for the interview and practice thoroughly, several times.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interview performance is assessed on clarity of presentation, focus on scientific ideas, ownership of the research, ability to defend and discuss methodology and novelty, readiness to answer detailed questions, and adherence to interview rules and time. Avoid business-style slides and lengthy irrelevant detail; rehearse Q&A and logistics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outcome categories and eligibility to reapply
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals rejected (not invited A; B; C). Invited A proposals. A invited max. 44. A not invited — Can apply next year. B — Wait for 1 year. C — Wait for 2 years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Panel outcomes place proposals into bands (A, B, C) with different implications for invitation to Step 2/interview and re-application timelines. 'A invited' are invited to next stage; 'A not invited' may reapply next year; B and C have specified waiting periods before re-application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Common applicant mistakes / anti-patterns
rubrics_metrics.description: Mistakes: 1. Unsure/unconvincing about your own project (not your idea). 2. Provide vague/unnecessary long answers (wasting time). 3. Unaware of or 'hiding' recent or previous development in the field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid being uncertain about the novelty/ownership of your ideas, be concise and focused in answers (especially in interviews), and be transparent and up-to-date about recent work in the field. These are behaviours that reduce competitiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Communication of feedback to applicants
rubrics_metrics.description: Feedback to applicants. Writing panel comments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Panels must prepare written comments to communicate strengths/weaknesses and justify decisions; feedback follows the panel discussion and scoring, and is provided according to ERC feedback procedures.
